result:
It compiled successfully on the first try (deprecation/unchecked notes are just from raw `List`/`Set` usage and `new Integer(...)`, harmless under `-source 8`).

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/cli2/commandline/WriteableCommandLineImplAgentTest.java` as a self-contained JUnit 3.8 (`TestCase`) suite. Since `api/` only documents `WriteableCommandLineImpl` itself (not `Option`, `CommandLine`, or `WriteableCommandLine`), I built `Option` fixtures with `java.lang.reflect.Proxy` instead of guessing/hardcoding that interface's exact method set — the handler answers the methods the contract implies (`getPreferredName`, `getTriggers`, `getId`, `canProcess`, `findOption`, etc.) and gives type-safe defaults for anything else.

Coverage includes: empty-state invariants, `addOption`/`hasOption`/`getOptions`/`getOptionTriggers`, `addValue`/`getValues` (including the documented default-fallback and null-default edge case), `setDefaultValues` vs `getUndefaultedValues` distinction, `addSwitch`/`getSwitch`/`setDefaultSwitch`, both property namespaces (`addProperty`/`getProperty`/`getProperties` with and without an `Option`, including replacement semantics), `getOption`/`looksLikeOption` trigger lookup, and `getNormalised()`'s always-empty contract since nothing in the documented API mutates it.
